title: Home water store
summary: What a household needs to hold, carry and treat its water for the planning period.

items.text: Stored drinking water: at least 1 gallon (3.8 L) per person per day
items.note: Store more for children, nursing mothers, pregnant women, sick people, pets and hot weather.

items.text: Unopened bottled water, sealed in its original containers
items.note: The safest stored water. Counts toward the total above. Use before its expiration date.

items.text: Food-grade water storage containers or clean plastic soft drink bottles, with tight lids
items.note: Never milk jugs, glass, or anything that held chemicals.

items.text: Jugs small enough to carry when full, for fetching water and for leaving
items.note: A full 5-gallon jug weighs about 42 lb (19 kg).

items.text: Dish soap, to wash containers before filling
Plain, unscented household chlorine bleach (5% to 9%), stored at room temperature and less than a year old
items.note: For sanitizing containers and treating water. Never mix bleach with ammonia or any other cleaner.

items.text: Medicine dropper, for measuring bleach drops
Teaspoon measure, for the container sanitizing solution
Labels, grease pencil or crayon, to mark each container “Drinking water” with the date
A pot to boil water and a stove with fuel
items.note: Never use a portable gas camp stove or burn charcoal indoors.

items.text: Clean cloths, paper towels or coffee filters, to strain cloudy water
Portable water filter with an absolute pore size of 1 micron or smaller
items.note: Filters do not remove viruses: disinfect the water after filtering.

items.text: Know where the main water valve is, and keep a wrench by it if it needs one

sources.name: CDC, How to Create an Emergency Water Supply (reviewed June 27, 2025)
sources.used: 1 gallon per person per day; store more for pregnant women, sick people, pets, hot climate; bottled water safest, observe expiration date; food-grade containers, not glass; never containers that held toxic chemicals; wash with soap; 1 teaspoon bleach per quart sanitizing solution; label “drinking water” with date

sources.name: Ready.gov (FEMA), Water
sources.used: 1 gallon per person per day; children, nursing mothers and sick people need more; very hot temperatures can double needs; bottled water sealed in its original container

sources.name: American Red Cross, Survival Kit Supplies; American Red Cross, Disaster Supplies Kit (University of Missouri Extension EMW1012)
sources.used: One gallon per person per day; household liquid bleach; easy-to-carry kit; milk containers do not seal well

sources.name: National Disaster Education Coalition (American Red Cross, FEMA and others), Talking About Disaster: Disaster Supplies Kit
sources.used: Soft drink bottles; avoid milk cartons and glass bottles; household liquid bleach to treat drinking water; medicine dropper; shut-off wrench

sources.name: US EPA, Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water; CDC, How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency (reviewed September 19, 2024)
sources.used: Bleach 5% to 9%, unscented, less than a year old at room temperature (as in surv-make-water-safe); boiling the best way to kill germs; strain cloudy water through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter; portable filters need an absolute pore size of 1 micron or smaller for parasites and will not remove viruses, disinfect after filtering

sources.name: CDC, How to Safely Clean and Sanitize with Bleach (reviewed August 26, 2026)
sources.used: Never mix bleach with ammonia or any other cleaner

sources.name: CDC, Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning Basics
sources.used: Never use a portable gas camp stove indoors; never burn charcoal indoors

sources.name: University of Alaska Fairbanks Cooperative Extension, Emergency Water Supply (SAL-00006, 2021)
sources.used: Movable 3 to 6 gallon jugs; spare lids; mark the fill date with a crayon or grease pencil

sources.name: FEMA, American Red Cross and USDA, Food and Water in an Emergency
sources.used: Know the location of the incoming water valve

sources.name: USGS Water Science School, Facts About Water
